firmware.brief: Implement a visual reaction-time game, not the fixed focus timer. Use SSD1306 128x64 I2C on SDA GPIO21 and SCL GPIO22, auto-detect 0x3C then 0x3D. KY-040 push switch on GPIO25 is active-low with INPUT_PULLUP; configure GPIO26/27 as encoder inputs but ignore rotation. Show 'Press to start' at boot. A new button press starts a round; require button release stable for 20 ms before arming the waiting phase, so holding the start button cannot trigger a response. Display 'Wait...' and choose a fresh random delay uniformly from 2000 to 5000 ms using the ESP32 random source. Any falling edge during this waiting phase is a false start; display 'Too soon!' and offer another round after release. At expiry, display a large 'GO!' and begin reaction timing at completion of the cue's I2C transfer, using a monotonic microsecond clock. Capture the first button falling edge with a GPIO interrupt and timestamp it promptly, including while screen transfers run; do not delay timestamping for debounce. Handle captured edges at the cue boundary consistently, treating edges before cue transfer completion as false starts. Ignore subsequent switch bounce until released continuously for 20 ms. On a valid response display elapsed time rounded to integer milliseconds and session best valid result. If there is no response within 10 s, display 'No response' without updating best. Results remain visible until a fresh press starts the next round after stable release. Do not block button capture with display updates. Rotation has no effect. Keep all game state in RAM; no networking or persistent storage. Results are approximate because of OLED refresh latency and switch timing.

messages: A USB-powered reaction-time game with a screen and a push button that shows your response time and catches false starts.

The firmware runs a visual reaction-time game with interrupt-timestamped button presses, randomized waits, false-start detection, a ten-second timeout, and a RAM-only session best. A model wrote this firmware and it has only been compiled, so read it before you flash it.

firmware.brief: Use the temp-monitor board layout with custom humidity-only firmware. Initialize I2C on SDA GPIO21 and SCL GPIO22 at 100 kHz. Detect the BME280 at 0x76 or 0x77 and SSD1306 128x64 OLED at 0x3C or 0x3D. Measure relative humidity every 2 seconds and display a large rounded integer with '% RH' and a smaller 'Humidity' label. Do not display temperature or pressure and do not implement alarms or controls. Until the first valid measurement show 'Reading...'. On sensor initialization failure or invalid/failed readings, replace the number with '-- % RH' and 'Sensor error', retrying sensor initialization every 2 seconds until recovered; never retain a stale number as a current reading.

messages: A USB-powered desk display that shows room humidity on a small OLED screen.

The firmware detects the OLED and BME280 on 100 kHz I2C, displays rounded humidity every two seconds, and replaces failed readings with a sensor error while retrying initialization. A model wrote this firmware and it has only been compiled, so read it before you flash it.
